question: Select the option with the correct use of present tense.
option_1: She spended all her money on make-up in order to look beautiful.
option_2: She had spend all her money on make-up in order to look beautiful.
option_3: She spends all her money on make-up in order to look beautiful.
option_4: She has spend all her money on make-up in order to look beautiful.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. She spends all her money on make-up in order to look beautiful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Simple Present Tense is used to describe habitual actions, general truths, or facts, and is formed as: Subject + V1/V5 (verb + s/es for third person singular) + Object.

• Applying the rule: the subject "She" is third person singular, so the base verb "spend" must take the "-s" form, i.e. "spends".
◦ Correct: She spends all her money on make-up in order to look beautiful.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "spended" is not a valid verb form — the past tense of the irregular verb "spend" is "spent", not "spended".

• Option 2 is incorrect because "had spend" is grammatically wrong; the Past Perfect Tense requires "had + V3", i.e. "had spent", not "had spend".

• Option 4 is incorrect because "has spend" is grammatically wrong; the Present Perfect Tense requires "has/have + V3", i.e. "has spent", not "has spend".

NOTE

• "Spend" is an irregular verb: spend – spent – spent (V1 – V2 – V3).

• For third person singular subjects (he/she/it) in the Simple Present Tense, the verb takes -s/-es, e.g. runs, watches, goes.

question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
When it / come to football, / my brother is / an addict.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. come to football,

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "it", which is a third person singular pronoun, and the verb used with it must agree in number and person.

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement (Simple Present Tense): with third person singular subjects (he/she/it), the main verb takes -s/-es.

• Applying the rule: "it come" is incorrect; it should be "it comes".
◦ Correct sentence: When it comes to football, my brother is an addict.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "an addict." is correct as printed — no error.

• Option 3: "my brother is" is correct as printed — the singular subject "my brother" correctly takes the singular verb "is".

• Option 4: "When it" is correct as printed — no error.

NOTE

• The expression "when it comes to (something)" is a common idiomatic phrase meaning "regarding" or "in the matter of", e.g. "When it comes to cooking, she is an expert."

• Always check subject-verb agreement carefully in error-spotting questions — a common trick is a singular subject paired with a plural/bare verb form, or vice versa.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
Throw of / the old shoes; / nobody will wear / them now.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Throw of

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The intended meaning of the sentence is to discard the old shoes, which requires the phrasal verb "throw away" (to discard/get rid of something), not "throw of", which is not a correct English expression.

• Rule: "of" is a preposition, but it cannot combine with "throw" to form a meaningful phrasal verb; the correct particle here is "away".
◦ Correct sentence: Throw away the old shoes; nobody will wear them now.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "them now." is correct as printed — no error.

• Option 2: "nobody will wear" is correct as printed — no error.

• Option 3: "the old shoes;" is correct as printed — no error.

NOTE

• Common confusion pairs in SSC error-spotting: "throw away" (discard) vs "throw of" (not valid); "throw up" (vomit / give up); "throw out" (eject / discard).

• Always check whether the preposition/particle used with a verb forms a genuine phrasal verb with the intended meaning.

question: Select the option with the correct use of article(s).
option_1: I was rude to him when I was in an fit of rage.
option_2: I was rude to him when I was in fit of rage.
option_3: I was rude to him when I was in the fit of rage.
option_4: I was rude to him when I was in a fit of rage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. I was rude to him when I was in a fit of rage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiomatic expression is "in a fit of rage" (in a sudden, uncontrolled burst of anger), which always takes the indefinite article "a" before "fit" because "fit" here is a singular countable noun being introduced for the first time (not a specific, already-known one).

• Rule — Articles: use "a" before a singular countable noun beginning with a consonant sound; use "an" before a singular countable noun beginning with a vowel sound; use "the" only for a specific, already-identified noun.

• Applying the rule: "fit" begins with a consonant sound /f/, so it takes "a", not "an" or "the"; and the article cannot be omitted altogether since "fit" is a singular countable noun here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "an fit" is wrong — "fit" begins with a consonant sound, so it must take "a", not "an".

• Option 2 is incorrect because the article has been omitted altogether; a singular countable noun like "fit" must be preceded by an article.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "the fit of rage" is wrong — "the" is used for something specific/already known, but here "fit of rage" is a general, non-specific expression requiring "a".

NOTE

• Other common idioms using "a fit of": a fit of anger, a fit of laughter, a fit of coughing, a fit of jealousy — all take the indefinite article "a".

• Remember: article choice depends on the sound, not the letter — e.g. "an hour" (silent h) but "a university" (sounds like "yoo").

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

During the days of slavery, there lived (1)_____ very hard-working slave. One day, (2)_____ freedom, he ran away from his masters house. As he passed a forest, he saw a lion (3)_____ with pain, for a huge thorn had pierced its paw. The slave felt sorry for the lion and took out the thorn gently. The grateful lion licked the slaves hand. But just then, both of (4)_____ were captured by the soldiers. The king ordered, “Let the runaway slave (5)_____ thrown in front of a hungry lion.” But, when the slave was thrown in front of the lion, the lion licked him and quietly sat beside him. The amazed king asked the reason. The slave told the king everything. The king pardoned the slave. The lion was also freed and sent to the forest.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires an indefinite article before the singular countable noun phrase "very hard-working slave", since the slave is being introduced for the first time in the passage (not a specific, already-known person).

• Rule — Articles: use "a" before a word/phrase beginning with a consonant sound, and "an" before a word/phrase beginning with a vowel sound. Here, the very next word after the blank is "very", which begins with the consonant sound /v/.

• Applying the rule: since "very" begins with a consonant sound, the correct article is "a", giving "there lived a very hard-working slave".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "the" is incorrect because "the" is used for a specific/already-identified noun, but the slave is being mentioned for the first time here.

• Option 3: "an" is incorrect because "an" is used before a vowel sound, but "very" begins with a consonant sound.

• Option 4: "two" is incorrect because the passage refers to a single slave, not two, and "two" would not fit the sense of the sentence.

NOTE

• Article choice is always based on the sound of the immediately following word, not necessarily the noun itself, since an adjective may intervene (e.g. "a very hard-working slave", "an extremely bright student").

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

During the days of slavery, there lived (1)_____ very hard-working slave. One day, (2)_____ freedom, he ran away from his masters house. As he passed a forest, he saw a lion (3)_____ with pain, for a huge thorn had pierced its paw. The slave felt sorry for the lion and took out the thorn gently. The grateful lion licked the slaves hand. But just then, both of (4)_____ were captured by the soldiers. The king ordered, “Let the runaway slave (5)_____ thrown in front of a hungry lion.” But, when the slave was thrown in front of the lion, the lion licked him and quietly sat beside him. The amazed king asked the reason. The slave told the king everything. The king pardoned the slave. The lion was also freed and sent to the forest.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. to gain

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank expresses the purpose behind the slave's action of running away, i.e. the reason he ran away.

• Rule — Infinitive of Purpose: to express the purpose of an action, English uses "to + base verb (V1)", e.g. "He worked hard to succeed."

• Applying the rule: the purpose of running away was "to gain freedom", so the infinitive "to gain" correctly fills the blank.
◦ Correct: One day, to gain freedom, he ran away from his masters house.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "gain" is incorrect because a bare base verb cannot stand alone here to express purpose without "to".

• Option 2: "gains" is incorrect because a finite, subject-agreeing verb form does not fit this non-finite purpose clause.

• Option 4: "gained" is incorrect because the past tense form does not express purpose; it would incorrectly suggest a completed action rather than an intention.

NOTE

• The infinitive of purpose ("to + V1") can also be replaced by "in order to" or "so as to" for the same meaning, e.g. "He ran away in order to gain freedom."

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

During the days of slavery, there lived (1)_____ very hard-working slave. One day, (2)_____ freedom, he ran away from his masters house. As he passed a forest, he saw a lion (3)_____ with pain, for a huge thorn had pierced its paw. The slave felt sorry for the lion and took out the thorn gently. The grateful lion licked the slaves hand. But just then, both of (4)_____ were captured by the soldiers. The king ordered, “Let the runaway slave (5)_____ thrown in front of a hungry lion.” But, when the slave was thrown in front of the lion, the lion licked him and quietly sat beside him. The amazed king asked the reason. The slave told the king everything. The king pardoned the slave. The lion was also freed and sent to the forest.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. roaring

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank describes an ongoing action/state of the lion at the moment the slave saw it — the lion was in the continuous act of roaring because of the pain.

• Rule — Present Participle (V-ing) as a Descriptive Modifier: when describing an action happening simultaneously with the main action of the sentence (here, "he saw a lion..."), the present participle form (V-ing) is used.

• Applying the rule: "he saw a lion roaring with pain" correctly uses the participle "roaring" to describe the lion's ongoing action at the time it was seen.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "roars" is incorrect because a finite present-tense verb cannot be used here; the sentence already has its main verb "saw", and this position requires a non-finite participle describing the lion.

• Option 2: "roared" is incorrect because the simple past form cannot function as a participial modifier of "lion" in this structure.

• Option 3: "roar" is incorrect because the bare base form cannot describe an ongoing action of the noun "lion" in this position.

NOTE

• Present participles (V-ing) are commonly used after "saw/heard/noticed" + object to describe an action in progress, e.g. "I saw him running", "She heard the baby crying".

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

During the days of slavery, there lived (1)_____ very hard-working slave. One day, (2)_____ freedom, he ran away from his masters house. As he passed a forest, he saw a lion (3)_____ with pain, for a huge thorn had pierced its paw. The slave felt sorry for the lion and took out the thorn gently. The grateful lion licked the slaves hand. But just then, both of (4)_____ were captured by the soldiers. The king ordered, “Let the runaway slave (5)_____ thrown in front of a hungry lion.” But, when the slave was thrown in front of the lion, the lion licked him and quietly sat beside him. The amazed king asked the reason. The slave told the king everything. The king pardoned the slave. The lion was also freed and sent to the forest.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. them

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires an object pronoun referring back to "both", which stands for the slave and the lion together — i.e. two entities, requiring a plural pronoun.

• Rule — Pronoun-Antecedent Agreement: a pronoun must agree in number and person with the noun(s) it refers to. Since it refers to two beings (the slave and the lion), the plural object pronoun "them" is required.

• Applying the rule: "both of them were captured" correctly refers to the slave and the lion together.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "her" is incorrect because it is a singular, feminine pronoun and does not agree with the plural antecedent (slave + lion).

• Option 2: "him" is incorrect because it is singular and would refer to only one of the two beings, not both.

• Option 3: "us" is incorrect because it is a first-person plural pronoun, but the passage is narrated in the third person; "us" would wrongly include the narrator/speaker.

NOTE

• "Both of" is always followed by a plural pronoun/noun, e.g. "both of them", "both of us", "both of the boys" — never a singular form.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

During the days of slavery, there lived (1)_____ very hard-working slave. One day, (2)_____ freedom, he ran away from his masters house. As he passed a forest, he saw a lion (3)_____ with pain, for a huge thorn had pierced its paw. The slave felt sorry for the lion and took out the thorn gently. The grateful lion licked the slaves hand. But just then, both of (4)_____ were captured by the soldiers. The king ordered, “Let the runaway slave (5)_____ thrown in front of a hungry lion.” But, when the slave was thrown in front of the lion, the lion licked him and quietly sat beside him. The amazed king asked the reason. The slave told the king everything. The king pardoned the slave. The lion was also freed and sent to the forest.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. be

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the causative structure "Let + object + bare infinitive", where "let" is followed directly by the base form of the verb (without "to"), and here the required action is passive in meaning — the slave is to be thrown to the lion.

• Rule — Causative "Let" with Passive Bare Infinitive: "Let + object + be + V3" is used to express permission/command for something to be done to the object, e.g. "Let the work be finished."

• Applying the rule: "Let the runaway slave be thrown in front of a hungry lion" correctly uses the bare infinitive passive form "be thrown".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "been" is incorrect because "been" is a past participle used with "has/have/had", not directly after "let + object".

• Option 2: "being" is incorrect because the continuous form "being thrown" does not fit the causative "let + object + bare infinitive" structure, which requires the simple base form "be".

• Option 4: "is" is incorrect because a finite verb "is" cannot follow "let + object" in this bare-infinitive causative construction.

NOTE

• The causative "let" pattern: Let + object + V1 (base form) for active meaning (e.g. "Let him go"), and Let + object + be + V3 for passive meaning (e.g. "Let the door be closed").

question:
Identify the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence.
A boisterous horse must have a rough bridle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Calm.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Boisterous" means noisy, rowdy, and full of energy in an uncontrolled or unruly way. (शोरगुल मचाने वाला/उछल-कूद करने वाला)
◦ Example: The boisterous children ran wildly around the playground.

• Its antonym is "Calm", which means quiet, peaceful, and free from excitement or disturbance. (शांत)
◦ Example: After the storm, the sea became calm again.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Rowdy" (उपद्रवी): noisy and disorderly — this is a synonym, not an antonym, of "boisterous".

• Option 2: "Loud" (तेज़ आवाज़ वाला): producing a lot of noise — also a synonym of "boisterous", not its opposite.

• Option 3: "Bouncy" (उछलने वाला): full of energy and enthusiasm — again close in meaning to "boisterous", not opposite.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "boisterous": unruly, rambunctious, exuberant, noisy.

• Other antonyms of "boisterous": quiet, gentle, subdued, placid, serene.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement required’.
I am so glad that I ran into you on the way.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. No improvement required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "ran into" means to meet someone unexpectedly or by chance.

• In the sentence, the speaker expresses happiness at having unexpectedly met the listener — this is precisely the meaning conveyed by "ran into", so the sentence is already correct as printed.
◦ Correct: I am so glad that I ran into you on the way.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "ran over" is incorrect because it means to knock someone down with a vehicle, which does not fit the happy context of the sentence.

• Option 3: "ran away" is incorrect because it means to flee or escape, which changes the meaning entirely and does not fit the context of being glad to meet someone.

• Option 4: "ran out of" is incorrect because it means to have no more of something left (e.g. "ran out of time"), which is unrelated to meeting someone.

NOTE

• Other common phrasal verbs with "run": run into (meet by chance), run over (hit with a vehicle), run out of (exhaust supply of), run away (flee), run after (chase), run down (criticize / become weak).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Stingy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Generous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Stingy" means unwilling to spend money or give things away; miserly. (कंजूस)
◦ Example: He is too stingy to buy anyone a gift.

• Its antonym is "Generous", which means willing to give freely; open-handed. (उदार/दानशील)
◦ Example: She is very generous and always helps those in need.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Humorous" (हास्यप्रद): funny, amusing — unrelated in meaning to "stingy" or its opposite.

• Option 3: "Lascivious" (कामुक): feeling or showing an open interest in sexual activity — unrelated to "stingy".

• Option 4: "Deceitful" (धोखेबाज़): dishonest, misleading — unrelated to "stingy".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "stingy": miserly, tight-fisted, mean, parsimonious, niggardly.

• Other antonyms of "stingy": generous, liberal, charitable, magnanimous, munificent.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the following sentence.
The arrival of Pragati in the house brought disharmony among the family members.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Rift in the lute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Rift in the lute" means a small flaw, disagreement, or discord that spoils an otherwise happy or harmonious relationship/situation. (रिश्ते में दरार/मनमुटाव)
◦ Example: Their long friendship suffered its first rift in the lute when they disagreed over money.

• The sentence describes Pragati's arrival causing disharmony (discord/disagreement) among family members, which is exactly the sense conveyed by "rift in the lute".

• The phrase originates from Tennyson's line "It is the little rift within the lute, that by and by will make the music mute" — a small crack in a lute (a musical instrument) that eventually spoils its music, symbolising a small discord that ruins a relationship.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Tenterhooks" (उत्कंठा/बेचैनी): to be in a state of suspense or anxious anticipation — unrelated to disharmony.

• Option 2: "A cry in the wilderness" (निर्जन में पुकार): a request or warning that is ignored by everyone — unrelated to disharmony.

• Option 4: "Hair breadth" (बाल बराबर अंतर): a very narrow margin (usually "a hair's breadth") — unrelated to disharmony.

NOTE

• Other idioms related to family/relationship conflict: "bone of contention" (a cause of dispute), "bad blood" (long-standing hostility), "to fall out with someone" (to quarrel with someone).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Titanic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Huge.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Titanic" means of exceptional size, strength, or power; enormous. (विशाल/बहुत बड़ा)
◦ Example: The workers made a titanic effort to finish the project on time.

• Its synonym is "Huge", which also means extremely large in size or amount. (बहुत बड़ा)
◦ Example: They live in a huge mansion on the hill.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Deep" (गहरा): extending far down or in from a surface — describes depth, not overall size, so it is not a true synonym.

• Option 3: "Attractive" (आकर्षक): pleasing in appearance — unrelated to size.

• Option 4: "Disastrous" (विनाशकारी): causing great damage — this is likely a distractor confusing "titanic" with the sinking of the ship Titanic, but the word itself means "huge", not "disastrous".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "titanic": colossal, immense, gigantic, massive, enormous, mammoth.

• The word derives from the Titans, the giant deities of Greek mythology, and gave its name to the ill-fated ship RMS Titanic because of its huge size.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
Prajakta is a very vain girl.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Humble.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Vain" means having an excessively high opinion of one's own appearance, abilities, or achievements; conceited. (घमंडी/अभिमानी)
◦ Example: He is too vain to admit that he was wrong.

• Its antonym is "Humble", which means having a modest or low estimate of one's own importance; not proud. (विनम्र)
◦ Example: Despite her success, she remained humble and down-to-earth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Honourable" (सम्माननीय): deserving honour and respect — unrelated to vanity/pride.

• Option 3: "Honest" (ईमानदार): truthful, not deceptive — not a direct opposite of "vain".

• Option 4: "Hopeful" (आशावान): feeling or inspiring optimism — unrelated to vanity/pride.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "vain": conceited, arrogant, self-important, narcissistic.

• Other antonyms of "vain": modest, unassuming, unpretentious, self-effacing.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
Ralph's condition worsened in the hospital.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Improved.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Worsened" means became worse; deteriorated. (बिगड़ गया)
◦ Example: The patient's health worsened overnight.

• Its antonym is "Improved", which means became better. (सुधर गया)
◦ Example: His condition improved after the surgery.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Scaled" (चढ़ना/नापना): climbed or measured according to a scale — unrelated to becoming better or worse.

• Option 3: "Changed" (बदल गया): became different — this is too general and neutral; it does not specifically mean "became better", so it is not a true antonym.

• Option 4: "Traversed" (पार किया): travelled across or through something — unrelated to health/condition.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "worsen": deteriorate, decline, aggravate, degenerate.

• Other antonyms of "worsen": improve, recover, ameliorate, better.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.
This win could enhance to be a historic turning point in the fortunes of the team.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. prove.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "Enhance" means to increase or improve the quality/value of something, and it is not followed by a "to be" infinitive construction — it does not fit the structure "enhance to be...".

• Rule: the verb "prove" is correctly used in the structure "could prove to be", meaning "could turn out to be" — this is the standard idiomatic construction for predicting an eventual outcome.

• Applying the rule: "This win could prove to be a historic turning point..." correctly expresses that the win may eventually turn out to be significant.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "demonstrate" is incorrect because "demonstrate to be" is not an idiomatic English construction; "demonstrate" is normally followed directly by an object or a "that" clause, not "to be".

• Option 3: "accomplish" is incorrect because "accomplish" means to complete or achieve something successfully; it does not fit the sense of "turning out to be" and is not used with "to be".

• Option 4: "confirm" is incorrect because "confirm to be" is not a standard English construction; "confirm" is typically followed by a noun/clause, not "to be".

NOTE

• The construction "could/may/might + prove + to be + noun phrase" is a common SSC-tested pattern meaning "may eventually turn out to be", e.g. "The decision proved to be a wise one."

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Fasten
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Bolt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Fasten" means to close or attach something firmly so that it is secure; to fix in place. (कसना/बांधना)
◦ Example: Please fasten your seatbelt before the flight takes off.

• Its synonym is "Bolt", which as a verb means to fasten or secure something firmly, typically with a bolt or lock. (सांकल/कुंडी लगाना)
◦ Example: He bolted the door before going to sleep.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Loosen" (ढीला करना): to make less tight — this is the opposite of "fasten", not a synonym.

• Option 3: "Undo" (खोलना): to unfasten or reverse something that has been done — this is also opposite in meaning to "fasten".

• Option 4: "Detach" (अलग करना): to disconnect or separate something — again opposite in meaning to "fasten".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "fasten": secure, attach, fix, tie, lock, clasp.

• Other antonyms of "fasten": loosen, undo, detach, unfasten, release.

question:
There is a spelling error in the given sentence. Select the option that contains the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
The precious bookshelf was carefully decorated with religiuos books.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. religiuos.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "religious" — relating to or believing in a religion. (धार्मिक)
◦ Example: They follow strict religious customs during the festival.

• Spelling key: RELIGI + OUS. The word ends in the common adjective suffix "-ious", spelt i-o-u-s; the printed word "religiuos" wrongly swaps the order to u-o-s.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "precious" is correctly spelt — meaning of great value.

• Option 2: "decorated" is correctly spelt — meaning made more attractive by adding ornamental features.

• Option 3: "carefully" is correctly spelt — meaning in a careful manner.

NOTE

• Many SSC spelling questions test the suffix "-ious" (religious, mysterious, spacious, gracious) versus the similar-sounding "-eous" (courageous, gorgeous) and "-uous" (continuous, strenuous) — always check the exact vowel sequence.

question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options.
The committee heard that he had been negliegent in his duty.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. negligent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "negliegent" as printed in the sentence is misspelt; the correct spelling is "negligent" — failing to give proper care or attention to one's duties; careless. (लापरवाह)
◦ Example: The negligent driver was fined for speeding through the red light.

• Spelling key: NEGLI + GENT. Note the sequence "g" before "e" and no "ie" combination — the printed error wrongly inserts an extra "e" before "gent" as "negliegent".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "dutie" is itself an incorrect spelling of "duty"; the sentence already correctly spells "duty", so this option is irrelevant to the actual error.

• Option 3: "comittee" is itself an incorrect spelling of "committee" (it needs a double "m" and double "t"); the sentence already correctly spells "committee", so this option is irrelevant.

• Option 4: "hurd" is itself an incorrect spelling of "heard"; the sentence already correctly spells "heard", so this option is irrelevant.

NOTE

• The word "negligent" is related to "negligence" (noun) and "negligible" (adjective meaning "so small as to be not worth considering") — do not confuse the two.

• Always first locate the actual misspelt word in the given sentence before checking the options; some options may themselves be wrongly spelt versions of correctly-spelt words in the sentence, added as distractors.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.
Mothers have great animosity for their children.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. affection.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Animosity" means strong hostility or hatred, which contradicts the natural, loving relationship between mothers and their children described in the sentence — hence it is the wrong word choice here.

• The correct word required by the context is "Affection", meaning a gentle feeling of fondness or love, which correctly describes what mothers feel for their children.
◦ Correct sentence: Mothers have great affection for their children.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "absurdity" means something ridiculous or illogical — this does not fit the context of a mother's feelings for her children.

• Option 3: "affectation" means an unnatural or pretended manner adopted to impress others — this is unrelated to the genuine emotion described here, and is a near-homophone trap for "affection".

• Option 4: "abasement" means the action of lowering someone in rank, dignity, or estimation — this is unrelated to a mother's feelings for her children.

NOTE

• "Animosity" is close in sound to several other words that are frequently confused in SSC exams — always check the meaning fits the context, not just the sound.

• Words that are similar in spelling/sound but very different in meaning (like "affection" vs "affectation") are common SSC traps — always read carefully.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The CEO's decision to cut benefits was a __________ move.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. harsh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes a decision to cut benefits, which is generally viewed as a severe, unkind, or strict action affecting employees negatively.

• The word "Harsh" means severe, strict, or unpleasantly rough in effect, which correctly matches the negative connotation of cutting benefits.
◦ Correct sentence: The CEO's decision to cut benefits was a harsh move.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "humorous" means funny or amusing — this does not fit the serious, negative context of cutting benefits.

• Option 3: "rigorous" means thorough, extremely careful, or demanding (typically describing a process, method, or standard) — it does not naturally describe a decision that negatively affects people in this way.

• Option 4: "laborious" means requiring considerable time and effort — this describes difficulty of a task, not the severity/unkindness of a decision, so it does not fit the context.

NOTE

• Context clues are key in fill-in-the-blank vocabulary questions: a negative action (cutting benefits) requires a word with a matching negative connotation.

• Words often confused with "harsh": stern, severe, strict (similar meaning) vs. mild, gentle, lenient (opposite meaning).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Sonam's cat used to chase the mouse into the kitchen and knock through a tower of pots and pans.
option_1: knock inside a tower of pots
option_2: knock over a tower of pots
option_3: knock away a tower of pots
option_4: knock out a tower of pots
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. knock over a tower of pots.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "knock over" means to hit something/someone causing it to fall down, which correctly describes a cat colliding with a stack of pots and causing them to topple.
◦ Example: The cat knocked over the vase while chasing the mouse.

• The underlined phrase "knock through" is not a standard, meaningful phrasal verb combination in this context and does not correctly convey the idea of pots falling down.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "knock inside a tower of pots" is incorrect because "knock inside" is not a meaningful phrasal verb and does not convey the sense of pots toppling over.

• Option 3: "knock away a tower of pots" is incorrect because "knock away" means to remove something by hitting it, which does not correctly describe a whole tower of pots falling down.

• Option 4: "knock out a tower of pots" is incorrect because "knock out" means to render unconscious or eliminate (e.g. in boxing/competitions), which does not fit the physical image of pots falling over.

NOTE

• Other common phrasal verbs with "knock": knock over (cause to fall by hitting), knock down (demolish/cause to fall), knock out (render unconscious/eliminate), knock off (stop working / reduce price), knock up (prepare quickly, British usage).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The organisation's furtive actions must be taken into notice and dealt with accordingly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Truthful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Furtive" means done secretly or stealthily to avoid notice; sly and secretive. (गुप्त/चोरी-छिपे किया गया)
◦ Example: He gave a furtive glance at the exam paper of the student sitting next to him.

• Its antonym is "Truthful", which means open, honest, and not hiding anything. (सच्चा/स्पष्ट)
◦ Example: She gave a truthful and open account of what had happened.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Futuristic" (भविष्यवादी): relating to or having ideas far ahead of the current time — unrelated in meaning to "furtive".

• Option 3: "Shady" (संदिग्ध/छायादार): of doubtful honesty; secretive — this is a synonym, not an antonym, of "furtive".

• Option 4: "Foxy" (चालाक): cunning or crafty — again a synonym, not an antonym, of "furtive".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "furtive": secretive, sneaky, stealthy, surreptitious, clandestine.

• Other antonyms of "furtive": open, honest, candid, forthright, transparent.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Cost an arm and a leg
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To be very expensive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Cost an arm and a leg" means to be extremely expensive; to cost a very large amount of money. (बहुत महंगा होना)
◦ Example: That designer handbag cost her an arm and a leg.

• The idiom exaggerates the price of something by comparing it to the enormous, unaffordable price of losing a limb, emphasising just how costly the item is.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "To be moderately priced" (उचित मूल्य पर होना): describes something reasonably priced — this is the opposite of the idiom's meaning.

• Option 2: "To be inexpensive" (सस्ता होना): describes something cheap — this is directly opposite to the idiom's meaning.

• Option 4: "To be affordable" (सामर्थ्य के भीतर होना): describes something within one's budget — again opposite to the idiom's meaning.

NOTE

• Other idioms meaning "very expensive": "cost a fortune", "cost a pretty penny", "pay through the nose", "break the bank".

• Idioms meaning "cheap/inexpensive" for contrast: "dirt cheap", "a steal", "for a song".
